what: Infinite scroll loads the next page of items automatically when the reader nears the end of the list. It combines an IntersectionObserver that watches a sentinel element with cursor-based pagination from the API.
like: Like a conveyor belt of sushi: a new plate rolls out just before the last one runs out, so you never ask for it.
why: Readers keep scrolling with no clicks or page reloads
Only the first page is fetched up front, so the initial load is small
Cursors keep the feed stable even when new items arrive

steps.d: Fetch the first page with a limit (for example 20 items) and render it. The response includes a cursor that points to where the next page starts.
Place a small empty element after the last item and observe it with IntersectionObserver. No scroll listener or throttling is needed.
Set rootMargin (for example '400px 0px') so the callback fires before the sentinel reaches the screen, and the next page arrives before the reader hits the end.
Call fetchNextPage; the query library sends after=cursor. Guard against double-firing by checking isFetching and hasNextPage.
Add the new page to the list, de-duplicating by item id, since new items may shift data between pages.
Virtualize long feeds or cap stored pages, restore scroll position on back navigation, and offer a Load more button so keyboard users and the footer stay reachable.

numbers.l: IntersectionObserver reports when a target crosses a threshold, with no per-scroll callback; rootMargin can trigger before it is visible
TanStack Query's example cap on pages kept in memory (also limits what is refetched)

numbers.v: First fetch, then one per page
numbers.l: A stale infinite query refetches pages one at a time from the first, to avoid stale cursors

choices.d: Offset (page=3) breaks when items are inserted: you see duplicates or skip rows. A cursor marks a point in the list, so it stays stable, and the server can change how it paginates. GraphQL's connection spec uses cursors.
Auto-load feels smooth for feeds. A button is better when the footer matters, for keyboard and screen reader users, and for pages people want to bookmark.
Keep all pages and virtualize, or cap with maxPages and refetch on scroll back. Pick based on how far users really scroll.
Store the scroll offset and the cursor in history state or the query cache so Back returns to the same spot, not the top.

instead.why: Pair with infinite scroll so the DOM does not grow with every page
Numbered pagination in the URL is linkable and keeps the footer reachable

breaks.d: Offset pagination shifts when new items are inserted at the top.
breaks.see: The same post shows twice, or one is skipped
breaks.fix: Use cursor pagination and dedupe by id on the client

breaks.d: The sentinel stays visible after a short page, or the observer is re-created on each render.
breaks.see: Network panel shows a burst of identical requests
breaks.fix: Check isFetching and hasNextPage, observe once, move the sentinel after the new items

breaks.d: The list state is lost on navigation.
breaks.see: User returns to the top after opening an item
breaks.fix: Cache pages, restore scroll offset, and keep the cursor in router state

say: I use cursor pagination so the feed stays correct when new items arrive, and an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel with a rootMargin so the next page is already loading before the reader reaches the end.
The pages live in an infinite query cache, deduped by id, and I virtualize or cap pages so memory and DOM do not grow forever.
I keep a Load more button as a fallback because auto-loading hides the footer and is awkward for keyboard users.

followups.q: Why not a scroll event listener?
followups.a: It fires constantly and often forces layout when you measure position. IntersectionObserver is asynchronous and fires only when thresholds are crossed, so it is cheaper and needs no throttling.

followups.q: How do you handle new items arriving at the top?
followups.a: Do not insert them under the reader. Show a 'new posts' pill, and merge on click. The cursor for older pages stays valid.

today: TanStack Query's infinite queries, IntersectionObserver and cursor-based connections (Relay spec) are the standard stack. Pair with virtualization or maxPages for long feeds, and keep a visible Load more fallback for accessibility.

check.q: Why is cursor pagination better than offset for feeds?
check.a: It stays stable when items are inserted
d: It is always faster to implement
check.why: A cursor marks a position in the data, so inserts do not shift later pages.

check.q: What triggers the next page in a modern implementation?
check.a: IntersectionObserver on a sentinel near the end
d: A scroll listener on window with no throttle
check.why: The observer fires only when the sentinel crosses the threshold, with no per-scroll work.

check.a: Starts loading before the sentinel is visible
d: Changes the page margin in CSS
check.why: It grows the root's bounding box, so the callback fires early.
